title: Kedgeree
subtitle: Smoked haddock and rice with curry spices and soft-boiled eggs
excerpt: Flaked smoked haddock, basmati rice, and soft-boiled eggs with onion, curry powder, and parsley. A British-Indian dish from the Victorian breakfast table that works equally well for brunch or supper.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kedgeree is a British adaptation of the Indian khichri, a dish of spiced rice and lentils. British officers in India replaced the lentils with smoked fish, added hard-boiled eggs, and the dish returned to Victorian Britain as an Anglo-Indian breakfast staple. It is now considered a quintessentially British dish. The original khichri survives as kitchri in South Asian cooking. Undyed smoked haddock is preferable to the bright yellow dyed version: the flavour is cleaner and the colour more natural.

recipeTools.notes: For the rice and the fish.

content.text: Poach the haddock gently in milk: the mild acid in the milk keeps the flesh tender. Remove any bones while flaking. The eggs for kedgeree should be soft-boiled, not hard-boiled: 7 minutes gives a set white and a slightly jammy yolk. Add the fish at the very end to avoid breaking it up too much.

Place the haddock skin-side down in a wide pan. Pour over the milk. Add the bay leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer and poach for 8 minutes until the fish flakes. Remove the fish, discard the skin and any bones, and flake into large pieces. Reserve the poaching milk.
Soft-boil the eggs for 7 minutes. Transfer to cold water. Peel and halve.

Cook the rice according to packet instructions. Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 10 minutes until golden and soft. Add the curry powder and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute.

Add the cooked rice and 100 ml of the reserved poaching milk. Stir to combine. Gently fold in the flaked haddock. Add the lemon juice and parsley. Season with salt. Top with the halved eggs. Serve immediately.
